'''Massoud Kaviany''' is an Iranian-American mechanical engineer who has worked on heat transfer fundamentals, heat transfer physics, and multiscale energy-transport phenomena. He is a professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering and the Applied Physics Program at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name="UMichME">{{cite web |title=Massoud Kaviany |url=https://me.engin.umich.edu/people/faculty/massoud-kaviany/ |access-date=20 November 2025 |publisher=University of Michigan}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Kaviany was born in 1948 in Tehran, Iran, and moved to the United States in 1968. He earned a B.S. (1973) and M.S. (1974) in energy engineering from the [[University of Illinois Chicago]].<ref name="UMichME" /> He completed his Ph.D. in mechanical engineering at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1979 under the supervision of R. A. Seban.<ref name="UMichME" />

== Career ==
Kaviany worked as a staff scientist at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] from 1979 to 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Massoud Kaviany |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37318498900 |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org}}</ref> In 1981, he joined the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee as an assistant professor, becoming associate professor in 1985.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Massoud Kaviany |url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/ME/People/HawkinsLecture/Hawkins_2005.pdf |website=engineering.purdue.edu}}</ref> He moved to the [[University of Michigan]] in 1986, where he became full professor in 1992.<ref name="UMichME" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Massoud Kaviany {{!}} U-M LSA Applied Physics Program |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/appliedphysics/people/faculty/kaviany.html |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=lsa.umich.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
=== Phonon transport ===
Kaviany's work on [[lattice vibrations]] addresses [[phonon scattering]], mean free paths, and thermal conductivity in crystalline and amorphous solids, with applications to thermoelectric materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Essentials of Heat Transfer |url=https://assets.cambridge.org/97811070/12400/frontmatter/9781107012400_frontmatter.pdf |website=assets.cambridge.org}}</ref> He advanced a "[[phonovoltaic]]" concept, a [[p–n junction]] capable of converting hot optical phonons into electrical power, and introduced "phonocatalysis," in which atomic-scale vibrations drive molecular dissociation at surfaces.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Melnick |first=Corey |last2=Kaviany |first2=Massoud |date=2016 |title=Phonovoltaic. I. Harvesting hot optical phonons in a nanoscale p -n junction |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016PhRvB..93i4302M/abstract |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=93 |issue=9 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.93.094302 |issn=0163-1829}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

His group also carried measurements of thermal conductivity in metal–organic frameworks, supported by classical molecular-dynamics simulation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Huang |first=B. L. |last2=McGaughey |first2=A. J. H. |last3=Kaviany |first3=M. |date=2007-02-01 |title=Thermal conductivity of metal-organic framework 5 (MOF-5): Part I. Molecular dynamics simulations |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931006005473 |journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer |volume=50 |issue=3 |pages=393–404 |doi=10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2006.10.002 |issn=0017-9310|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Electron transport and energy conversion ===
Kaviany has conducted parallel investigations into electronic transport, electron–phonon coupling, and nanoscale heat transfer, particularly for thermoelectric devices and micro–thermoelectric coolers. Contributions include a melting-induced thermal-conductivity switch, analysis of interflake thermal conductance of graphene, and the concept of heterobarrier phonon recycling.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kim |first=Kwangnam |last2=Kaviany |first2=Massoud |date=2016-10-17 |title=Thermal conductivity switch: Optimal semiconductor/metal melting transition |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.94.155203 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=94 |issue=15 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.94.155203 |issn=2469-9950|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Fluid–particle transport and phase change ===
His work has informed water management in fuel-cell electrolyte layers, boiling and critical heat flux, and the enhancement of thermal conductance using porous coatings.<ref>{{Citation |last=Kaviany |first=Massoud |title=Fluid Streams in Two-Phase Systems |date=2001 |work=Principles of Convective Heat Transfer |pages=135–178 |editor-last=Kaviany |editor-first=Massoud  |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-3488-1_3 |isbn=}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Kaviany |first=Massoud |title=Solid-Fluid Systems with Large Specific Interfacial Area |date=2001 |work=Principles of Convective Heat Transfer |pages=349–415 |editor-last=Kaviany |editor-first=Massoud  |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-3488-1_5 |isbn=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Huang |first=Bao-Ling |last2=Kaviany |first2=Massoud |date=2008 |title=Ab initio and molecular dynamics predictions for electron and phonon transport in bismuth telluride |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.77.125209 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=77 |issue=12 |article-number=125209 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.77.125209 |issn=1098-0121|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Discuss |first=D_o_S |date=2007-06-21 |title=Asetek signs research agreement with Professor Massoud Kaviany |url=https://www.techpowerup.com/33420/asetek-signs-research-agreement-with-professor-massoud-kaviany |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=TechPowerUp |language=en}}</ref>
